title: Rule of Rose
subtitle: A hierarchy written in red crayon
summary: Rule of Rose is Punchline's PlayStation 2 psychological-horror game, first released in Japan on 19 January 2006. Set in Britain in 1930, it follows Jennifer into a world controlled by girls who have organised themselves as the Red Crayon Aristocrats. Their demands and social rules give the adventure an oppressive structure, making humiliation and exclusion part of its fear. Jennifer searches for meaning within this uncertain world with the help of her dog, Brown. The game builds its unease around childhood memories and the power that a group can exercise over somebody outside it.
body: Rule of Rose is Punchline's PlayStation 2 psychological-horror game, first released in Japan on 19 January 2006. Set in Britain in 1930, it follows Jennifer into a world controlled by girls who have organised themselves as the Red Crayon Aristocrats. Their demands and social rules give the adventure an oppressive structure, making humiliation and exclusion part of its fear. Jennifer searches for meaning within this uncertain world with the help of her dog, Brown. The game builds its unease around childhood memories and the power that a group can exercise over somebody outside it.

Brown can follow the scent of objects, helping Jennifer locate items needed to continue. The partnership gives exploration a practical relationship rather than leaving the dog only as a figure in the story. Finding what the children demand can mean searching spaces that remain difficult to understand, while encounters expose Jennifer's vulnerability. The player gradually assembles connections between objects, places and memories. That process supports the psychological horror: an ordinary possession can acquire a disturbing significance because of the circumstances in which it is requested, found or remembered.

Punchline developed the project after Sony requested a horror game, drawing on fairy tales and an interest in the uncertain world of childhood. Yutaka Minobe's score was performed by studio musicians, giving the atmosphere a deliberately human texture. Rumours about its content caused a moral panic before the European release and contributed to cancellation in the United Kingdom. Reviews were mixed, particularly about the gameplay. The game's later reputation rests more on its story, music and imagery, which leave the player interpreting the cruelty and memories behind Jennifer's experience.
